summary: Richland County, SC tower built by the CCC in 1936 for Columbia's sesquicentennial; SC Forestry Commission operated it until 1993; NHLR-registered 2012; a park friends post says it is no longer safe to climb.

access.note: Inside a public state park; a Friends of Sesqui post says the tower is no longer safe to climb. No official closure notice found; restricted level is our inference from that post.

notes_for_editor: Brief record checks out: built 1936 and registered October 2, 2012 match NHLR. Left out of the story: a StoryMaps search result (storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/c7196e87d7af47e2a90c4eb79831e87e) says the tower was first built at Fort Jackson and moved to the park in 1940. Fetch returned only the page title, and a WebSearch on the claim found nothing confirming it, so it needs a human check; it conflicts with NHLR's 1936 build at this site. The Friends of Sesqui post is undated in our copy and is the only source on climbing safety; its comment thread (not used) mentions the tower being dismantled, which is unverified. Access level restricted is our inference. No fire history found. Fact-check 2026-10-09: the Register's 1936 build date is a year before the 1937 land purchase in Wikipedia, so the story now says the two are not reconciled. The story also uses the agency's full name and footnotes the park-celebration sentence, which had none.
